minutes.summary: The Lunenburg School Committee opened by thanking the town for passing special town-meeting override funding that is already reducing second-grade class sizes, then heard a superintendent's report on literacy initiatives and a new primary classroom. Most of the meeting was spent publicly interviewing a candidate for school business administrator (a position the committee itself hires and will vote on the following week), hearing principals' start-of-school updates, ratifying a cafeteria workers' contract, discussing a possible town-funded financial/process audit of the business office, and reviewing (but deferring votes on) operating protocols and committee goals, including the Turkey Hill Elementary MSBA process and a primary school parking lot/playground study.
minutes.headline: The school committee will hire its own next business administrator, deciding by vote next week after tonight's public interview.

what_happened.line: The school committee will vote next week on hiring a school business administrator, after publicly interviewing a candidate tonight.
The school department will ask the town finance committee to fund a financial and process audit of the school business office from the town's reserve rather than the school budget.
The committee ratified a new three-year contract for cafeteria workers.
Votes on committee operating protocols and this year's goals, including the Turkey Hill Elementary MSBA process, were pushed to next week.
The chair said override funding approved at the recent special town meeting is already being used to reduce second-grade class sizes.

why_it_matters: The business administrator runs school finance day to day, and the committee itself controls this hire and expects to decide it next week.
The proposed audit's funding source determines whose budget absorbs the cost, and it goes to the town finance committee for a decision, not the school committee.
The Turkey Hill Elementary MSBA process is an early procedural step that can lead toward a future building project and a town vote.
